slides.texte_overlay:
How to become a more
patient man
Notice what makes you impatient. Traffic, slow replies, queues. Knowing your triggers is the first step to staying calm when they happen.
Breathe out before you react. One long exhale gives your brain the second it needs to choose a better response. Practise it daily.
Expect things to take longer. Add twenty percent to every plan. Most frustration comes from unrealistic timelines, not from real problems.
Practise waiting without your phone. In line, at the doctor's, at a red light. Sitting with a little boredom builds patience like a muscle.
Before: I wanted results instantly. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I learned that small steps add up over time.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I wanted results instantly. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I learned that small steps add up over time.

slides.texte_overlay: Learn a slow skill. Gardening, woodworking, an instrument. Skills that take months teach you to enjoy progress instead of rushing it.
Be patient with people. Everyone is fighting battles you don't see. A little grace makes you calmer and makes others trust you more.
